content: 1. A study published in the Brazilian Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2010 (Volume 14, Pages 594–600) examined the epidemiology of infectious diseases in Eastern Brazil. 2. Cerda R et al. analyzed the healthcare utilization and costs associated with a support program for patients co-infected with HIV and tuberculosis in Peru. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases in 2011 (Volume 15, Pages 363–368). 3. Hermans SM et al. demonstrated that integrating HIV and TB services in a large urban HIV clinic in Uganda led to improved TB treatment outcomes and earlier initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART). This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012 (Volume 60, Pages e29–e35). 4. Howard A et al. discussed the role of PEPFAR in scaling up collaborative TB/HIV activities. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012 (Volume 60, Pages S136–S144). 5. Huerga H et al. evaluated the impact of introducing HIV testing, treatment, and care in a rural TB clinic in Kenya. The results were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases in 2010 (Volume 14, Pages 611–615). 6. Kerschberger B et al. conducted a before-and-after study to assess the effect of fully integrating HIV and TB services on the time to ART initiation. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2012 (Volume 7, Article e46988). 7. Lawn SD et al. investigated delays in starting ART among patients with HIV-associated TB who accessed non-integrated clinical services in a South African township. This study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2011 (Volume 11, Article 258). 8. Louwagie G et al. explored missed opportunities for accessing HIV care among TB patients in Tshwane, South Africa, under different care models. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases in 2012 (Volume 16, Pages 1052–1058). 9. Pevzner E et al. evaluated the rapid scale-up of collaborative TB/HIV activities in TB facilities in Rwanda between 2005 and 2009. The results were published in BMC Public Health in 2011 (Volume 11, Article 550). 10. Phiri S et al. shared their experience with integrated TB and HIV care in a resource-limited setting at the Martin Preuss Centre in Malawi. This study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2011 (Volume 16, Pages 1397–1403). 11. Bygrave H et al. presented lessons learned from implementing a TB/HIV one-stop shop model at primary healthcare clinics in rural Lesotho. This was shared at the XVIII International AIDS Conference in Vienna, Austria, in July 2010. 12. Chifundo K et al. discussed the best models for TB/HIV service delivery based on experiences from Malawi. 13. Dube C et al. examined the impact of scaling up ART services on TB services in rural Zambia. Their findings were presented at the XVIII International AIDS Conference in Vienna, Austria, in July 2010. 14. Howard AA et al. found that on-site TB services were associated with improved TB screening among HIV-infected patients enrolling in HIV care programs across six sub-Saharan African countries. 15. Ikeda J et al. reported that integrating HIV and TB services reduced mortality among indigenous populations in rural Guatemala. 16. Kaplan R et al. assessed the impact of providing ART in TB facilities in Cape Town, South Africa, on TB treatment outcomes. Their findings were presented at the 43rd Union World Conference on Lung Health in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in November 2012. 17. Morse J et al. evaluated integrated TB/ART clinics in Lusaka, Zambia, focusing on enrollment into HIV care and early ART initiation among TB/HIV co-infected patients. This was presented at the 43rd Union World Conference on Lung Health in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in November 2012. 18. Mugo P et al. shared experiences of integrating TB and HIV care services at a rural district hospital in Kenya. This was presented at the 40th Union World Conference on Lung Health in Cancun, Mexico, in December 2009. 19. Muvuma S et al. conducted a retrospective cohort study in rural Zambia, highlighting poor linkages between TB and HIV services and their impact on care quality, from HIV testing to ART initiation. 20. Odhiambo J et al. described models of TB-HIV integration and their achievements in Nyanza Province, Kenya. This was presented at the 43rd Union World Conference on Lung Health in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in November 2012. 21. Schwartz A et al. conducted a retrospective cohort study in Botswana, comparing outcomes among HIV-positive adults with active pulmonary TB treated in clinics with and without on-site HIV services. 22. Mathers MB et al. performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on mortality among people who inject drugs, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2013 (Volume 91, Pages 102–123). 23. Yan Zhao et al. investigated the impact of methadone maintenance treatment on mortality among HIV-positive people who inject opioids in China. This study was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2013 (Volume 91, Pages 93–101). 24. Achmad Y et al. conducted a cohort study in Bandung, Indonesia, on integrating methadone maintenance treatment and HIV care for injecting drug users. The findings were published in Acta Medica Indonesiana in 2009 (Volume 41, Supplement 1, Pages 23–27). 25. Lucas G et al. compared clinic-based treatment for opioid-dependent HIV-infected patients with referral to an opioid treatment program in a randomized controlled trial. This study was published in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2010 (Volume 152, Pages 704–711). 26. Zaller N et al. proposed a model of integrated primary care for HIV-positive patients with underlying substance use and mental illness, published in AIDS Care in 2007 (Volume 19, Pages 1128–1133). 27. Fatti G et al. evaluated ART outcomes at primary healthcare facilities in South Africa, comparing three tiers of ART services. This study was published in PLoS One in 2010 (Volume 5, Article e12888). 28. Bock P et al. examined the provision of ART to children within South Africa's public sector, published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2008 (Volume 102, Pages 905–911). 29. Humphreys CP et al. compared nurse-led, primary care-based ART with hospital care in Swaziland in a controlled prospective study, published in BMC Health Services Research in 2010 (Volume 10, Article 229). 30. Assefa Y et al. assessed the effectiveness and acceptability of ART delivery by health officers and nurses in Ethiopian health centers, published in the Journal of Health Services Research and Policy in 2012 (Volume 1, Pages 24–29). 31. Brennan AT et al. evaluated outcomes of stable HIV-positive patients down-referred from doctor-managed ART clinics to nurse-managed primary health clinics in South Africa, published in AIDS in 2011 (Volume 25, Pages 2027–2036). 32. Chan AK et al. assessed the decentralization of ART provision in rural Malawi using an integrated primary care model, published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2010 (Volume 15, Supplement 1, Pages 90–97). 33. Balcha TT and Jeppsson A compared ART outcomes between hospitals and health centers in Ethiopia, published in the Journal of the International Association of Physicians in AIDS Care in 2010 (Volume 9, Pages 318–324). 34. Bedelu M et al. described the implementation of ART in rural communities using the Lusikisiki model of decentralized HIV/AIDS care, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2007 (Volume 196, Supplement 3, Pages S464–S468). 35. Massaquoi M et al. examined patient retention and attrition on ART at the district level in rural Malawi, published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2009 (Volume 103, Pages 594–600). 36. Jaffar S et al. compared virological failure rates in patients treated in home-based versus facility-based HIV care models in Uganda in a cluster-randomized equivalence trial, published in The Lancet in 2009 (Volume 374, Pages 2080–2089). 37. Kipp W et al. reported results of a community-based ART program for HIV-1 infection in western Uganda, published in Current HIV Research in 2010 (Volume 8, Pages 179–185). 38. Selke HM et al. evaluated task-shifting of ART delivery from healthcare workers to people living with HIV/AIDS in a community-based program in Kenya, published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2010 (Volume 55, Pages 483–490). 39. Fairall L et al. conducted a cluster-randomized trial on task-shifting ART management from doctors to primary-care nurses in South Africa (STRETCH), published in The Lancet in 2012 (Volume 380, Pages 889–898). 40. Sherr KH et al. compared the quality of HIV care provided by non-physician clinicians and physicians in Mozambique in a retrospective cohort study, published in AIDS in 2010 (Volume 24, Supplement 1, Pages S59–S66). 41. Sanne I et al. conducted a randomized non-inferiority trial comparing nurse versus doctor management of HIV-infected patients receiving ART in South Africa (CIPRA-SA), published in The Lancet in 2010 (Volume 376, Pages 33–40).
